journal.text: Quill agreed to ninety up front.
Quill hired you to lift Mara Voss's unedited hour from Glass Chapel.
The choir door accepted a name you kept on a chip.
Mara Voss signed the Ward Nine coolant dump. Three hundred people, one memo.
A second copy of Mara's hour exists.
Mara authorized her own current statement for the private Ward Nine records desk only. Lumen did not endorse it. No public release, witness permission or historical authentication was supplied.
You tell her Quill paid for the original and the other file went into circulation. Mara heard this account from you in the clinic. It supplies no new source or permission.
After telling Mara what happened to her hour, you acknowledged choosing your part in it. She accepted a personal conversation, without forgiving it or granting public quotation.
Mara says she wants a morning in which she chooses what she remembers. This is her present hope, not an observed treatment outcome or an acquittal.

You paid fifteen creds for private courier dispatch and stayed with Mara while she turned her cup toward the window. The dispatch and shared hour supplied no desk answer, acquittal, clinic endorsement or witness permission.

Mara's separately authorized, named private statement was dispatched to the Ward Nine records desk. It contained no worker list or clinic endorsement. Receipt and any inquiry decision remain unobserved.
The Ward Nine records desk acknowledged receiving Mara's named private response into an unanswered queue. No inquiry finding, historical authentication, acquittal or public release followed.
You returned to Mara's personal conversation about the hour. This visit supplied no inquiry result or new public permission.
